digest.component_or_area: CLI parser foundation and help generation
propositions: Current CLI parsing is fragmented across multiple ad-hoc argparse implementations, imperative argv loops, and hand-maintained help files, causing drift between documented, runtime, and generated syntax.
A centralized argparse factory protocol with a frozen route registry must enforce that all command grammars are produced by a single side-effect-free factory used at runtime.
Generated package help and grouped overview must be byte-deterministic, validated during build, and served before operation/config/store/handler boundaries.
Parser migrations must maintain backward compatibility and parity in accepted/rejected argv, diagnostics, exit codes, and streams; retired syntax remains unknown and undiscoverable.
All command family parsers (core, advanced, bridge, reconciler, LLM, workflow, audit, identity) must be migrated atomically with their runtime handlers from imperative parsing to shared factories.

Help routing and alias handling must use generated artifacts exclusively, with compatibility shims composing canonical helpers to preserve historical command spellings while preventing docs-only or regex-based grammar duplication.
